correctness.rationale: Exact graph adjacencies and closed neighborhoods were reconstructed directly. For omitted sets of size at most seven, the proof shows nonadjacent pairs cannot fail 2-sharp separation, while adjacent failures are exactly four-vertex forbidden configurations; two-domination separately excludes six omissions in a closed neighborhood. Full enumeration of omitted sets and independently coded complete detector-set evaluations agree on all coefficients, including impossibility of seven omissions. Explicit full-automorphism enumerations and graph-exchange neighbor construction prove orbit sizes and component counts; breadth-first distances certify rook exchange diameter six and an explicit 16-mask adjacency isomorphism together with automorphism images certifies all six small Shrikhande components. All three included sources were executed from the final scientific paths and asserted each number. The claim is restricted to the two finite graphs and does not infer an infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The 2022 criterion addresses asymmetric false-negative identification but does not compute the two specified sixteen-vertex graphs. The 2015 strongly regular graph study, the 2021 redundant-identification variant, and the accessible published ordinary identifying-code/locating-domination comparison of the Shrikhande and rook pair use other sensor constraints, with weaker or noncomparable set families. Exact polynomial coefficients and minimum-code exchange components are not entailed by known minima or common strongly regular parameters. Other known results on the same two graphs concern different notions. No exact or dominating source was found after the listed searches and inspections; the residual risk of an unindexed covering computation is acknowledged. The result is original under available evidence, not independently priority-certified.

value.rationale: The nonisomorphic canonical strongly regular Shrikhande–rook pair is a motivated comparative testbed. Ordinary identifying-code minimum sensor requirements differ, yet the more robust one-false-negative problem has equal minimum cost ten and sharply different optimum multiplicity and reconfiguration connectivity (connected versus 23 components). The unique finite forbidden-four-set families (324 versus 396), complete polynomials, exact automorphism orbits, and rook-component isomorphisms supply independently useful structural information for fault-tolerant locating sensor placement. It is not a simple substitute of a known scalar bound, nor a claim about arbitrary graph samples.
